description: Australian population age distribution based on ABS estimated resident population, June 2025.

reference.source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, National, state and territory population, Table 59: Estimated Resident Population by Single Year of Age, Australia.

notes: Age-group weights are derived from national population estimates.
Age groups: infant 0-1, preschool 2-4, school_age 5-11, adolescent 12-17, working_age_adult 18-64, older_adult 65+.
Hearing profile, onset, progression and auditory functional status remain uncalibrated simulation assumptions.
Geographical weights are read from the experiment configuration.
Auditory functional status is sampled independently of audiometric profile.
Measured hearing status and self-reported hearing status are independent, uncalibrated simulation assumptions.
Exact ages are sampled from ABS June 2025 single-year population counts; the 100+ category is represented as age 100.

measured_hearing_prevalence.source: Australian Eye and Ear Health Survey 2025
measured_hearing_prevalence.measurement: Bilateral hearing impairment measured using better-ear four-frequency pure-tone average.

hearing_aid_use_prevalence.source: Australian Eye and Ear Health Survey 2025
hearing_aid_use_prevalence.population: Survey participants aged 50 years and over
hearing_aid_use_prevalence.measurement_condition: Measured bilateral hearing impairment using better-ear four-frequency pure-tone average
notes: Reported hearing-aid use represents ever-use, not necessarily current use.
Rates apply to the specified measured impairment groups aged 50 years and over.
No rate is assumed for people without measured bilateral impairment or for people under 50.

self_reported_hearing_prevalence.source: Australian Eye and Ear Health Survey 2025, Table 47, Q1
self_reported_hearing_prevalence.question: Do you feel you have a hearing loss?
self_reported_hearing_prevalence.population: Survey participants aged 50 years and over
self_reported_hearing_prevalence.measurement_condition: Measured bilateral hearing impairment using better-ear four-frequency pure-tone average, greater than 25 dB HL
notes: This binary response is separate from the simulator's graded self_reported_hearing_status categories.
A report of hearing loss without bilateral impairment above 25 dB HL is not necessarily a false positive; unilateral or other hearing difficulty may not be captured by this measurement.
